Issued at 144 AM MDT Sun Sep 27 2026

Things are relatively quiet here at the humble Riverton weather 
abode early this Sunday morning. We will have some active weather in 
the forecast, but also a decently long period of fairly nice early 
autumn weather, so there is a little bit for everyone, depending on 
your taste.

The active weather will be front loaded. Most of the day today 
should be fairly quiet, although a few showers will be possible,
With the greatest number in the afternoon and in and near the 
mountains. However, a vast majority of the area should remain 
rain-free through the daylight hours. The main cause of the 
active weather, a shortwave that will be rotating around an 
upper level low over California, will begin making a closer 
approach tonight, increasing the coverage of showers and 
thunderstorms. With the southwest flow ahead of the wave, the 
main area of showers and isolated thunderstorms will be across 
southern and western Wyoming, with drier conditions east of the
Divide where downsloping flow may keep a lot of the showers 
away. As for temperatures, they will remain above normal, but 
more cloud cover will keep them a few degrees cooler than on 
Saturday.

The most widespread showers and thunderstorms still look to be 
on Monday. The shortwave will be passing through Wyoming at that
point. There will also be some upper level support from the 
left front quadrant of a 90 knot jet streak that will be passing
across southeastern portions of the area. As for threats, 
locally heavy rain is possible. Precipitable water values will 
be from 125 to 150 percent of normal with the additional upper 
level forcing from the jet streak. However, instability may be 
limited as there could be a decent amount of sky cover around 
the area. In addition, there will be steering flow so storms 
will be of the moving variety. In addition, most locations have 
been mainly dry since last Sunday, so there is room in the soil.
So, although the threat of flooding is not zero, it is low. As 
for overall amounts, most of southern and western Wyoming has at
least a 1 in 2 chance of a tenth of an inch of QPF through 
Tuesday morning. Most of western Wyoming, especially the favored
south and southwesterly upslope flow locations, have at least a
1 in 2 chance of a quarter of an inch of QPF. The highest 
amounts would be in the highest elevations of the southwestern 
slopes, like the western Wind River Range and the southern 
Absarokas where locally over a half an inch or rain could fall. 
And, with low wet bulb zero levels, small hail may also be 
possible with the stronger storms. Most showers decrease after 
sunset with only isolated to scattered leftover showers after 
midnight. 

And we have to talk about the possibility of high elevation
snow. The 700 millibar temperatures do fall as low as 2 Celsius
later Sunday night and Monday morning, bringing snow levels 
down to around 9500 to 10000 feet. It would not surprise me to 
see some snowflakes on the higher passes like Beartooth or 
Togwotee. However, any accumulation would be above 11000 feet 
and even here it looks light. The only location with a greater 
than 1 in 2 chance of over an inch or snow is the highest 
elevations of the Wind River Range where impacts would be slim 
to none.

We then enter the mainly dry period of the forecast. At this point, 
we are around 90 percent sure that we will have a decent period of 
nice autumn weather. The one wild card is that will happen with the 
combination of the upper level low moving eastward from California 
when it interacts with the moisture from the remnants of Hurricane 
Polo after it makes landfall in Mexico. Almost all the ensemble 
members keep the moisture south and east of Wyoming, but a few 
try to bring the edge into southern Wyoming. We will watch this 
but odds are against it at this point. Temperatures should 
average above normal for the most part as ridging builds into 
the area. A brief is likely Wednesday night and Thursday as a 
weak cold front moves through the area. With the lack of 
moisture, it will likely only bring some clouds and some 
breezes. Temperatures then warm again for Friday and into 
Saturday. The next chance of showers would be later Saturday 
into Sunday with another trough and cold front approaching. 
There has been poor model consistency with this feature though, 
so confidence in the details this far out is very low.
